Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Mental Health position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. My background in behavioral health, healthcare administration, child protective services, and youth education has given me experience working with children and families, coordinating services, supporting staff, and managing competing priorities. I’m interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to build on my experience while contributing to a program that supports adolescents and their families.

In my roles as a Student Analyst and Registered Behavior Technician (RBT), I’ve gained hands-on experience with treatment planning, initial assessments and reassessments, skill acquisition goals, parent training, documentation, and tracking client progress. I’ve also collaborated with speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists, teachers, and other providers to help ensure clients receive consistent support. In addition, I’ve helped train and support other RBTs, which has strengthened my communication and teamwork skills and shown me the importance of setting clear expectations and maintaining consistency across a team.

My experience as a Health Assistant further developed my organizational and administrative skills. I handled insurance verification, benefits, claims, payments, and client inquiries while managing a high volume of calls and follow-ups. I regularly worked with English- and Spanish-speaking clients, answered questions, and helped them navigate processes that could sometimes be confusing or stressful. This role taught me how to stay organized, communicate effectively, and follow through on multiple responsibilities while providing a positive experience for clients.

I also bring experience as a Child Protective Investigator with the State of Florida, where I worked with families facing difficult circumstances, responded to sensitive situations, coordinated referrals, and addressed safety concerns. Along with my previous experience in education and youth services, this role strengthened my ability to remain calm during challenging interactions, build rapport with children and families, and balance empathy with appropriate boundaries. I understand how important it is to create a structured, supportive environment, especially when working with adolescents who may be experiencing emotional or behavioral challenges.

I’m continuing my education in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and plan to pursue my BCBA credential and a certificate in Organizational Behavior Management (OBM). I’m particularly interested in developing my skills in leadership, staff development, and improving program operations through evidence-based practices. I would be excited to bring my experience in behavioral health, coordination, and staff support to AWA while continuing to grow professionally.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.

Sincerely,
Josmari Arroyo

Behavioral health professional with experience across ABA, child welfare, and healthcare, bringing a strong foundation in client support, staff development, program coordination, and safety-focused practices. Skilled in training and supporting team members, coordinating with families and multidisciplinary professionals, maintaining accurate documentation, and managing competing priorities in fast-paced environments. Experienced in responding to behavioral challenges, navigating sensitive situations, and promoting consistency and accountability in service delivery. Holds a master’s degree in Special Education with an ABA concentration and a graduate certificate in Contemporary Theory in Mental Health Services, and is pursuing a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a concentration in child and adolescent counseling. Passionate about supporting effective program operations and creating structured, compassionate environments where adolescents and their families can thrive, while ensuring staff feel supported, empowered, and equipped to provide quality care.

Cover Letter: 

Dear Hiring Team,

I was excited to come across the Program Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy because it brings together several areas that have shaped my professional experience and career goals: behavioral health, team development, and supporting children and families. Through my work in ABA and child welfare, I have seen how much of a difference a well-organized, supportive environment can make in a young person's progress. I would love the opportunity to build on that experience by helping lead a program where compassionate care, clear expectations, and strong daily operations work together to support adolescents and their families.

Throughout my nearly five years in ABA, I have gained hands-on experience supporting children and families while helping ensure treatment programs are implemented consistently and effectively. In my role as a Student Analyst, I participated in client intakes and initial assessments, contributed to reassessments and treatment planning, reviewed clinical documentation and behavioral data, and supported parent training and collaboration with multidisciplinary providers. I also helped train and support RBTs, communicate expectations, and work through challenges that affected treatment implementation. These responsibilities taught me the importance of clear communication, staff accountability, consistency, and attention to detail, all of which I recognize as essential to managing daily operations in a PHP/IOP setting.

My experience as a Child Protective Investigator with the State of Florida further strengthened my ability to respond calmly to challenging situations, gather and document sensitive information, assess safety concerns, and communicate with families experiencing difficult circumstances. This role required sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to navigate competing priorities while remaining focused on the well-being of children. I believe these skills would translate well to supporting adolescents with behavioral and emotional needs, responding to unexpected challenges, and helping maintain a safe, structured program environment.

I also bring experience in healthcare administration, including insurance verification, client communication, and managing responsibilities in a fast-paced environment. Combined with my clinical documentation and coordination experience, this background has prepared me to approach operational responsibilities with organization, follow-through, and an understanding of how administrative processes affect the overall client experience. I understand that effective program operations require more than keeping schedules and tasks on track. They require a team that communicates well, understands expectations, follows established procedures, and works together to provide consistent care to clients and their families. I value creating a workplace where staff feel supported and equipped to succeed while also understanding the importance of accountability, collaboration, and maintaining high standards of care.

My educational background reflects my continued commitment to understanding and supporting children, adolescents, and families. I hold a master's degree in Special Education with a concentration in Applied Behavior Analysis, a graduate certificate in Contemporary Theory in Mental Health Services, and a bachelor's degree in Interdisciplinary Social Science with a concentration in Sociology and a minor in Psychology. I am also pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a concentration in child and adolescent counseling. These experiences have reinforced my interest in the connection between behavioral, emotional, and environmental factors and the importance of creating supportive systems around the individuals we serve.

I would be excited to bring my experience, work ethic, and passion for this field to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I take pride in being dependable, thoughtful, and solutions-focused, and I value creating environments where adolescents and families receive compassionate support and staff members feel encouraged to grow and do their best work. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that is committed to helping adolescents and their families navigate challenges, build skills, and make meaningful progress.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with the needs of your program.

Warm regards,
Josmari Arroyo

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Hiring Committee

Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in customer service, health insurance member support, account management, and remote work, along with my ongoing education in psychology, I have developed strong communication, organization, and interpersonal skills that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.

As a psychology student, I am building my understanding of human behavior and psychological well-being while pursuing my goal of applying that knowledge in a meaningful professional setting. I am particularly interested in opportunities that allow me to support individuals and families as they navigate mental health challenges and access appropriate treatment services. I understand that seeking treatment can be an emotional and overwhelming experience, especially for adolescents and their families, and I would welcome the opportunity to help make the admissions process as compassionate and supportive as possible.

My previous experience as a remote Member Services Representative with Aetna Health Insurance has prepared me well for a virtual position. In this role, I assisted members with Medicare Advantage plans, provided technical support for the company website, and followed up on concerns to resolve issues related to members' coverage. Working remotely required effective communication, self-motivation, organization, and the ability to manage responsibilities independently while maintaining a high standard of customer service. These skills would translate well to communicating with prospective clients and families, addressing questions, and helping individuals navigate the admissions process.

Additionally, my experience as an Account Manager with Discover Financial Services strengthened my ability to handle sensitive account information, resolve disputes, communicate with team members, and identify solutions to customer concerns. At Rumpke Waste & Recycling, I assisted customers with residential accounts, registered new customers for service, and followed up on unresolved issues. Across these positions, I developed a consistent approach to listening to concerns, communicating information clearly, and following through to ensure issues were addressed professionally.

In my current position as a Postal Vehicle Operator with the United States Postal Service, I am responsible for safely operating a 26-foot box truck and transporting mail between post offices. This role has reinforced my reliability, attention to detail, time management, and ability to work independently while meeting daily responsibilities.

I am excited about the possibility of bringing my professional experience, remote work skills, and psychology education to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to a team dedicated to helping adolescents and their families connect with the care and support they need. I believe my combination of customer service experience, problem-solving abilities, and genuine interest in mental health would allow me to make a positive contribution to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and educational goals align with the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position.

Sincerely,

Caitlin Davison

I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in joining the team at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a dedicated Mental Health Professional (NCE Passed) with over two decades of progressive experience spanning outpatient psychotherapy, multi-systemic therapy, child and family intervention, and substance abuse counseling, I am deeply aligned with your mission to provide specialized, compassionate care for adolescents and their families.

Sincerely,

October 29, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over 12 years of experience in corrections, case management, and rehabilitative services, I have developed strong skills in client engagement, assessment, crisis intervention, and connecting individuals with appropriate treatment and community resources. I believe this experience would allow me to contribute to your admissions team and support individuals and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

Throughout my career, I have worked closely with individuals experiencing substance use disorders, mental health concerns, and other challenges affecting their daily lives. As a Correctional Counselor with the Iowa Department of Corrections, I conducted individual meetings, assessed treatment needs, facilitated evidence-based programming, and coordinated referrals to community providers. My subsequent experience as a Probation and Parole Officer further strengthened my ability to manage a demanding caseload, maintain accurate documentation, and communicate effectively with individuals, families, and treatment professionals.

In my current role as a Community Navigator with St. Vincent de Paul, I assist individuals impacted by incarceration in accessing treatment, employment, housing, and other community resources. This work requires patience, empathy, and consistent follow-through, particularly when working with individuals who may be overwhelmed or uncertain about their next steps. My training in motivational interviewing and trauma-informed care has helped me approach these conversations without judgment while encouraging individuals to engage in services that support their needs.

What interests me most about this position is the opportunity to help individuals and families during what may be a difficult and emotional time. I understand the importance of making a positive first impression, listening carefully, explaining available services clearly, and ensuring that individuals do not feel lost in the process of seeking treatment. I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities independently, coordinating with outside providers, and maintaining confidential client information.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, communication skills, and commitment to helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could support the work of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Seth Good

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Clinical Psychology from the University of Central Florida, ongoing graduate studies in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Keiser University, and hands-on experience supporting children and adolescents with diverse emotional, behavioral, and educational needs, I am confident that I would bring compassion, dedication, and a valuable perspective to your organization.

Throughout my academic and professional journey, I have developed a strong passion for adolescent mental health, particularly helping young individuals navigate emotional challenges, trauma, behavioral difficulties, and personal development. My experience as an academic tutor has allowed me to work closely with students diagnosed with ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, PTSD, and other learning and behavioral challenges. Through these experiences, I have strengthened my ability to establish trust, demonstrate patience, adapt my communication style, and create supportive environments where young people feel understood, respected, and empowered.

In addition to my tutoring experience, my leadership involvement with Her Movement has strengthened my commitment to youth advocacy, mentorship, and community engagement. These opportunities have reinforced my belief that meaningful change begins when young people are provided with consistent support, positive guidance, and access to resources that promote emotional wellness.

As a graduate student pursuing a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, I am continuing to develop my knowledge of counseling theories, trauma-informed approaches, ethical practices, and culturally responsive care. My long-term professional goal is to specialize in child and adolescent mental health, and I am eager to contribute to an organization whose work aligns with that passion.

What distinguishes me as a candidate is my combination of academic preparation, practical experience, leadership, and genuine dedication to making a difference in the lives of young people. I recognize that adolescents facing mental health challenges need more than encouragement; they need consistency, empathy, accountability, and individuals who are committed to helping them recognize their strengths and achieve meaningful progress.

I would be honored to bring my skills, enthusiasm, and commitment to Adolescent Wellness Academy while continuing to grow professionally alongside your team. Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and dedication to adolescent mental health would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Sincerely,
Dajia “Legacy” Elmore
B.S. Clinical Psychology
M.S. Clinical Mental Health Counseling Candidate

I believe my combination of behavioral health admissions experience, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and compassionate approach would make me a valuable addition to Adolescence Wellness Academy. MULEDRIDE BELONY Behavioral Professional
470-364-0310 Millybelony@gmail.com Orlando Fl, Willing to relocate
 Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for a position within your organization where I can utilize my background in behavioral health, child and family services, applied behavior analysis, and case management to support individuals and families in meaningful ways. With a Bachelor of Science in Biopsychology and experience working across clinical, educational, behavioral, foster care, and community-based settings, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of individualized support, advocacy, communication, and compassionate care.
Throughout my professional experience, I have worked with children, adolescents, adults, and families with a variety of behavioral, developmental, mental health, and social-service needs. As a Registered Behavior Technician, I provided individualized 1:1 ABA services to children and adolescents ages 2–16, implementing skill-acquisition and behavior-support programs under BCBA supervision, collecting behavioral data, documenting progress, and supporting the development of communication, social, self-help, and adaptive skills. My experience in childcare and education also strengthened my ability to build relationships with children, provide structure, de-escalate challenging situations, and create supportive environments for learning and development.
My work with the Georgia Department of Family and Children Services further expanded my experience supporting children and families involved in the foster care system. I assisted case managers with supervised parent-child visitation, documented observations, supported children in community settings, and maintained professional and supportive relationships with families. In addition, my experience in behavioral program support and administration allowed me to develop skills in documentation, data management, staff support, program coordination, scheduling, and resource organization.
Most recently, my work in behavioral health case management has allowed me to support individuals and families experiencing mental health, housing, and other social-service needs. I have assisted clients with navigating resources, coordinating referrals, advocating for their needs, communicating with service providers, and maintaining appropriate documentation and follow-up. These experiences have strengthened my ability to look at the individual as a whole and recognize how behavioral health, family dynamics, community resources, and environmental factors can all impact a person's well-being.
I am particularly drawn to behavioral health because I value the opportunity to meet people where they are, build trust, and contribute to meaningful progress in their lives. I bring a combination of clinical exposure, behavioral experience, administrative skills, and genuine compassion for the individuals and families I serve. I am also committed to continuing my education and professional development within the behavioral health and social-service fields.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and passion for helping others could contribute to your organization and the individuals you serve.
Sincerely,
Muledride Belony

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinical Intake Specialist position. With a Master of Social Work degree and experience providing clinical services across outpatient, emergency department, and school-based settings, I bring a strong foundation in clinical assessment, risk evaluation, crisis intervention, and care coordination.

Throughout my clinical experience, I have conducted psychosocial and mental health assessments, evaluated suicide and self-harm risk, developed individualized safety plans, and identified appropriate treatment recommendations and referrals. My experience in the emergency department strengthened my ability to assess presenting concerns, recognize immediate safety needs, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to facilitate appropriate dispositions and continuity of care. In outpatient and school-based settings, I have further developed my ability to identify clinical needs, understand complex psychosocial factors, and support individuals and families in accessing appropriate services.

I am particularly interested in this position because it aligns with my strengths in clinical assessment, gathering relevant psychosocial information, determining service needs, and helping individuals navigate the treatment process. I understand the importance of conducting thorough, compassionate, and clinically informed intakes while ensuring that safety concerns are appropriately addressed and clients are connected with suitable levels of care.

In addition to my assessment and crisis intervention experience, I bring strong communication, documentation, and interdisciplinary collaboration skills. I am comfortable working with diverse populations, including children, adolescents, adults, and families, and approach each interaction with professionalism, empathy, and sound clinical judgment.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, assessment skills, and commitment to quality mental health care would contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Shannon Beaton

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in a Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern opportunity with your organization. I recently became a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (License #29789) and am seeking a clinical setting where I can provide individual therapy to children and adolescents. I bring more than 20 years of experience supporting children, teens, and families through counseling, crisis intervention, family engagement, and school-based mental health services.

I currently serve as a District Support Counselor with Broward County Public Schools, providing mental health and counseling support to approximately 43 elementary, middle, and high schools in the South Area.
